tasks.short: Audit payroll records, employer contributions and insurance coverage, then resolve exceptions and report findings.

steps.what: Define audit scope, periods, materiality and applicable employer obligations.
Export payroll transactions and employee records for the audit period.
Reconcile payroll totals and recalculate contributions using applicable rates, thresholds and dates.
Compare contracts and insurance documents with payroll classifications and coverage.

loop.input: Relevant contract clauses and insurance schedules, linked to employee records.
loop.output: Source-linked coverage fields and proposed discrepancies.
loop.check: Validate employee identifiers, dates and amounts; auditor checks ambiguous clauses before accepting findings.
loop.stop: Two extraction attempts per document; unreadable or conflicting clauses go to the auditor.
loop.why_not_simpler: Contracts and coverage clauses vary in wording; structured fields alone omit material exceptions.

steps.what: Discuss discrepancies and determine whether explanations or corrections satisfy the audit.
Prepare the audit report and supporting workpapers.

loop.input: Approved exception decisions, reconciliations and source-linked workpapers.
loop.output: Draft findings, limitations and recommendations in the audit template.
loop.check: Every figure ties to a workpaper; every finding cites evidence; unsupported statements are flagged.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass; unresolved gaps remain explicit for the audit lead.
loop.why_not_simpler: Case-specific explanations require prose beyond fixed report fields.

steps.what: Review evidence, approve conclusions and release the audit report.

tasks.design: A controlled job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} joins read-only extracts from the {PAYROLL}, {HCM} and {ERP}, then recalculates obligations using dated rules. Bounded document extraction links coverage exceptions to evidence in the {DOCS}; the {WORKFLOW} tracks decisions and prepares a report for audit-lead approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Identifiers, effective dates and coverage documents were fragmented. Maintaining jurisdiction-specific rules and evidence links cost more than writing the calculations.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding reduces connector and validation development effort. Bounded extraction can handle variable documents while arithmetic remains deterministic.
tasks.still_hard: Employment status, cross-border cases and disputed coverage require expertise. National rules differ; audit access must exclude unnecessary health and personnel details.
tasks.human_edge: The auditor judges whether classifications reflect actual employment arrangements and challenges explanations that appear technically consistent but misleading.

ambition.what: Quarterly review of employer contribution and coverage exceptions

tasks.altitude: The auditor spends less time assembling extracts and recalculating amounts, and more time resolving classification risks. Reporting frequency can increase; authority to change payroll or submit filings does not change.

reach.task: Forecast cash exposure from unresolved payroll liabilities.
reach.learn: Provisioning thresholds, scenario ranges and cash timing.

evidence.claim: Payroll reconciliation and contribution recalculation can use deterministic joins, dated rules and arithmetic; legal classification still needs judgement.
Baker Tilly Netherlands reported 40-50% savings on test of details using DataSnipper; this vendor case does not establish payroll-audit savings.

assumptions: The task is an audit of employer contributions and occupational insurance obligations applicable locally, rather than a direct transplant of US categories.
Time shares describe a periodic audit in a mid-size European organisation and are planning estimates.
The initial build covers one jurisdiction and read-only extracts; corrections and statutory submissions remain separate.
Build ranges include access review and any applicable employee consultation under national rules.
GDPR applies to personnel data; applicable EU AI Act duties depend on the intended use.
unknowns: Applicable jurisdictions, contribution schemes and insurance arrangements.
Availability of stable employee identifiers and historical rate tables.
Existing audit tools, export permissions and reviewer independence requirements.
Whether proposed processing triggers employee consultation under national rules.
research_questions: Which existing reconciliation controls can be configured before adding code?
Which clauses cannot be reliably represented as structured coverage fields?
What evidence and retention rules apply to this audit engagement?
new_work: Maintain dated rate tables and classification mappings.
Review ambiguous extraction and unmatched employee records.
Monitor extract completeness and reconcile source totals.
Maintain evidence permissions and resolve correction requests.

tasks.short: Assess whether management practices support organisational objectives and whether employees understand those objectives.

steps.what: Select objectives, business units and assessment questions.
Gather objectives, performance measures, management decisions and employee communication materials.
Interview managers and employees about priorities, trade-offs and practical understanding.
Map evidence and interview observations to each objective.

loop.input: Approved objectives, management documents and auditor-written interview notes.
loop.output: Source-linked observations grouped by objective, including contradictions and missing evidence.
loop.check: Auditor verifies citations and preserves dissenting observations; absence of evidence is not labelled employee misunderstanding.
loop.stop: Two passes over the approved evidence set; ambiguous mappings remain unclassified.
loop.why_not_simpler: Objectives and observations use different language and often imply relationships without shared identifiers.

steps.what: Judge alignment, employee understanding and the significance of conflicting evidence.
Challenge findings with management and agree accountable improvement actions.
Record approved conclusions, management responses and follow-up dates.

tasks.design: A scoped evidence register in the {WORKFLOW} links authorised records from the {DOCS}, {PROJECT} and {TALENT}. A bounded loop proposes an objective evidence map; the auditor conducts interviews and judges conclusions, while configured templates record approved findings and follow-up actions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Collecting evidence was fragmented, and interpreting alignment could not be reduced to objective completion scores. Interviews and organisational context remained essential.
tasks.enabler_now: Permission-aware retrieval and source-linked classification can reduce evidence preparation. Existing templates and action tracking can remove repeated report assembly.
tasks.still_hard: Employees may repeat official language without understanding trade-offs. Interview sampling, management pressure and confidentiality affect the validity of conclusions.
tasks.human_edge: The auditor creates enough trust to hear contradictions and distinguishes reasonable local trade-offs from management practices that undermine objectives.

ambition.what: A follow-up review of whether agreed management changes improved objective understanding

tasks.altitude: Most of the week still centres on interviews, judgement and management challenge. Preparation becomes lighter, enabling focused follow-up; management retains authority over objectives and organisational changes.

reach.task: Check whether budget allocations support the objectives identified in the assessment.
reach.learn: Budget ownership, resource constraints and the difference between stated and funded priorities.

evidence.claim: Templates, controlled evidence collection and action registers can reduce assessment administration.
Document classification can propose evidence mappings but cannot establish employee understanding or organisational alignment.

assumptions: This is an internal assurance assessment, rather than an individual employee performance rating.
Interviews remain human and use auditor-written notes; recording and automated transcription are outside the initial scope.
Only records relevant to the approved assessment are collected.
Build ranges include confidentiality arrangements, access and any consultation required by national rules.
GDPR applies to identifiable employee evidence; intended use must also be assessed under the EU AI Act.
unknowns: Whether objectives are documented and management records are accessible.
Existing employee consultation arrangements and restrictions on interview notes.
Whether employees can speak confidentially without managers receiving attributable comments.
Who approves findings and owns follow-up actions.
research_questions: Which evidence demonstrates practical understanding rather than familiarity with slogans?
What sampling approach gives credible coverage of units, shifts and seniority?
Can existing permissions support a confidential assessment evidence register?
new_work: Review proposed evidence mappings and contradictory observations.
Maintain objective versions and evidence access.
Remove unnecessary personal detail from reports.
Track whether agreed actions changed management practice.

tasks.short: Audit developing systems against financial requirements, controls and migration expectations before implementation.

steps.what: Define audit scope, financial risks and readiness criteria.
Provide design documents, configurations, migration mappings and existing test evidence.
Design independent tests for controls, accounting treatments and failure scenarios.
Execute test transactions and inspect access, approvals and accounting outputs in the test environment.
Reconcile migrated balances and compare observed outputs with independently calculated expectations.
Assess unresolved defects, control gaps and limitations against readiness criteria.
Challenge remediation plans and clarify residual risks with project and process owners.
Compile, review and issue the pre-implementation audit opinion.

tasks.design: A test harness on the {DATA_PLATFORM} executes approved scenarios against an isolated {ERP} test environment and independently reconciles balances and outputs. Evidence and defects link into the {PROJECT}, while a configured {DOCS} template assembles the audit opinion for approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Audit tests were rebuilt for each project, and environments or configurations changed during testing. Independent expected results and reproducible evidence required substantial setup.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding makes adapters, repeatable test fixtures and reconciliation scripts cheaper to build. Versioned configurations and existing test interfaces provide reproducibility where available.
tasks.still_hard: A passing test set cannot establish that the right risks were tested. Environment differences, incomplete requirements and late configuration changes can invalidate evidence.
tasks.human_edge: The auditor identifies missing failure scenarios and judges whether residual risk makes the system unsuitable for its intended financial use.

ambition.what: Readiness reassessment after each material configuration or migration change

tasks.altitude: The auditor spends less time replaying transactions and checking balances, and more time challenging test coverage and residual risk. The auditor retains the assurance opinion; the project sponsor retains implementation authority.

reach.task: Validate that migrated reporting definitions preserve financial meaning.
reach.learn: Data lineage, metric definitions and reconciliation across reporting layers.

evidence.claim: Repeatable transactions, independent expected results and deterministic reconciliations can automate financial-system test execution.
Risk selection, test adequacy and readiness opinions remain judgement work; the digest provides no direct implementation-audit case.

assumptions: The representative engagement concerns a financial system or a program affecting accounting records.
An isolated test environment supports repeatable execution without production writes.
Expected results are approved independently of the implementation team's calculations.
The first build covers a limited set of financial processes and one target environment.
Build ranges include environment access and any consultation required by national rules; GDPR and applicable EU AI Act obligations remain relevant.
unknowns: Test interfaces, environment availability and configuration stability.
Whether financial requirements and migration mappings are sufficiently explicit.
Availability of masked or synthetic test data.
Required audit independence and implementation approval arrangements.
research_questions: Which existing test facilities can be configured before building a harness?
How will expected results remain independent of implementation logic?
Which production differences must be checked before relying on test-environment evidence?
new_work: Maintain test fixtures and independent expected results.
Version test evidence against configurations and migration runs.
Investigate failed runs and distinguish defects from environment faults.
Retest affected controls after material changes.

tasks.short: Advise clients on compensation, benefits, accounting systems or long-range tax planning using evidence and financial scenarios.

steps.what: Clarify the client's objectives, constraints, jurisdiction and requested advice.
Request and assemble financial records, policy documents and relevant client facts.
Research applicable rules, guidance and effective dates for the advice topic.

loop.input: Engagement questions and an approved, dated collection of relevant guidance.
loop.output: Candidate applicable provisions, conditions, exclusions and source references.
loop.check: Accountant verifies jurisdiction, effective dates, source passages and applicability before calculation or advice.
loop.stop: Two passes through the approved collection; unresolved interpretation goes to a qualified specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Guidance expresses conditions in prose that cannot all be matched through fixed fields.

steps.what: Calculate costs, tax effects and sensitivities for defined options.
Select a recommendation and identify uncertainties, trade-offs and specialist referrals.
Explain options and test the recommendation against the client's priorities.
Draft the advice memorandum with assumptions, calculations and implementation dependencies.

loop.input: Accountant-selected recommendation, client preferences, validated calculations and checked rule references.
loop.output: Draft advice memorandum with explicit assumptions and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Figures must match calculation workpapers; citations must resolve; the draft cannot add options or legal conclusions.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass; unsupported passages remain flagged for the accountant.
loop.why_not_simpler: Explaining client-specific trade-offs requires tailored prose beyond a standard calculation report.

steps.what: Review and approve the memorandum, then send it to the client.

tasks.design: Configured intake in the {WORKFLOW} collects evidence into the {DOCS}, while deterministic calculators on the {DATA_PLATFORM} produce dated, reproducible scenarios. Bounded loops retrieve candidate rule passages and draft the memorandum; the accountant validates applicability, conducts the advice conversation and approves external release through the {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each engagement combined different facts, jurisdictions and advice topics. Calculations were reusable, but evidence gathering and explanation remained bespoke.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding reduces the cost of maintaining narrow scenario calculators and intake flows. Source-linked retrieval and constrained drafting reduce preparation without replacing professional interpretation.
tasks.still_hard: Long-range assumptions, changing national rules and interactions between benefits, employment and tax remain difficult. Estate planning and specialised benefits questions can require separately qualified advisers.
tasks.human_edge: The accountant uncovers unstated priorities, explains uncertainty and recognises when a financially attractive option conflicts with the client's wider interests.

ambition.what: A scheduled sensitivity review of an existing compensation or tax-planning recommendation

tasks.altitude: The accountant spends less time rebuilding calculations and writing first drafts, making more room for scenario discussions. They can recommend a wider range of tested options; client implementation rights and professional limits remain unchanged.

reach.task: Translate an approved planning scenario into filing requirements and evidence needs.
reach.learn: Filing deadlines, documentation standards and the boundary between planning assumptions and reportable facts.

evidence.claim: AFAS Jonas assists with income and corporate tax returns while the user remains responsible; this supports a narrow assistance pattern, not autonomous broad advice.
Defined financial scenarios can use deterministic calculators, while suitability and legal applicability require professional judgement.
The proposed intake, calculation and memorandum workflow is a design estimate; the digest provides no direct case for this combined advisory task.

assumptions: An engagement addresses one selected advice topic; it does not cover every topic in the occupational statement.
The client is a business decision-maker or an authorised individual receiving advice from a qualified accountant.
The first build supports one topic and jurisdiction using approved guidance and calculators.
Health-benefit advice uses plan and cost information without collecting individual medical records.
Build ranges include client-data access and any consultation required for employee-related changes under national rules.
GDPR applies to personal data; EU AI Act obligations depend on whether the eventual use extends into regulated employment decisions.
unknowns: The advice topic, client type, jurisdiction and required professional qualifications.
Availability and licensing of current authoritative guidance.
Existing validated calculators and engagement approval procedures.
Whether employee-level data or external specialist review is required.
research_questions: Which advice topic has stable enough rules and sufficient demand for the first calculator?
Which assumptions materially change the recommendation and deserve explicit sensitivity ranges?
What review standard and professional boundary apply before advice is released?
new_work: Validate extracted rule passages and maintain effective dates.
Maintain calculators, assumptions and regression examples when rules change.
Review draft explanations against approved recommendations.
Handle incomplete intake, specialist referrals and scheduled advice updates.

role.altitude: The role shifts from assembling evidence and repeating calculations towards testing assumptions, challenging explanations and communicating risk. Accountants retain responsibility for advice and auditors retain responsibility for assurance conclusions; implementation decisions stay with authorised owners.
reach: Financial managers: turn unresolved findings into quantified exposure and remediation priorities.
Budget analysts: compare stated objectives with funded activity.
Business intelligence analysts: trace financial measures through migrations and reporting layers.
Tax preparers: connect planning recommendations to filing evidence and deadlines.
skills_to_grow: Design deterministic reconciliations with independent expected results.
Maintain dated rules, data lineage and reproducible evidence.
Validate bounded extraction and drafting against source records.
Assess GDPR, applicable EU AI Act duties and national consultation requirements.
role.ambitious_version: Provide recurring, evidence-linked assurance and scenario reviews between major audits or advisory engagements, with explicit scope, independent checks and professional judgement at consequential decisions.
